01_objective_comparison: Schedule weights, not QUBO energies. Final CSP/MWIS objectives coincide for each matched input; hollow CSP markers reveal the overlap. Shared baseline is reused, not replicated.
02_average_terminal_size: Arithmetic means across all exported non-empty terminal QUBOs, including alternative branches later discarded. Both axes use common binary-QUBO units, not CSP satellite-variable counts versus MWIS contact-vertex counts.
03_runtime_breakdown: CSP hardware/environment provenance is incomplete and sampling budgets differ, so these are recorded timings rather than a controlled speed comparison. Total is the sum of producer and annealing notebook elapsed times; launcher/orchestration overhead is excluded. *CSP 100/50 lacks full notebook clocks: its bar contains only the producer stopwatch and its total is N/A. CSP does not save separate sampling/reconstruction clocks; the annealing notebook remainder combines them with setup/export overhead after subtracting MILP/LP solver time. Producer phases are disjoint; nested component timings and pipeline totals are not added twice. Frozen-input generation time is not measured here.
04_logical_qubo_dimensions: Binary variables and nonzero quadratic couplers for sampled terminals. Repeated (variables, couplers) pairs are aggregated; marker area increases with frequency. These are logical dimensions, not physical qubits, chains, chain lengths or embedding overhead. No hardware embedding was performed.
05_pre_milp_quality_gap: 100 × (certified final optimum − reconstructed pre-MILP weight) / certified final optimum. Computed only after confirming final objective equals the saved upper bound. This is the actual retrospective gap for these inputs, distinct from the looser pre-MILP conservative bound. Final certified gaps are zero.
06_final_schedule_provenance: Origins traced through the saved decomposition and sampled selections, then replaced by MILP provenance only for affected components. Exact preprocessing and separator choices are classical. Shares measure retained contacts/weight, not CPU work or quantum advantage. A sampled terminal discarded by reconstruction or MILP contributes no retained share.
07_sampling_and_decomposition: Counts include all alternative branches exported as non-empty terminal QUBOs. Total reads are summed from actual annealing_results.csv rows; per-terminal budgets are 500 for MWIS and 1,000 for CSP. Retention uses final terminal IDs, not contact counts. Incomplete leaves are all unresolved branches, not the count selected in the final schedule; zero is kept explicitly.
08_component_structure: Component sizes use candidate contacts in both methods, rather than CSP satellite variables versus MWIS contact vertices. CSP has already applied global dominance; this MWIS campaign has not. Means include singleton components, so the largest component is shown alongside them. These are root components before recursive separator decomposition, not terminal QUBOs or incomplete leaves.
09_quality_through_stages: Original schedule weights divided by the certified optimum of each input. The percentage axis is zoomed, with the same limits in every panel. Classical reference comes from the saved producer solution and is independently validated; sampled reconstruction comes from the saved tree/read results. Final hybrid may require no MILP for a complete run. In this campaign reference and sampled objectives match in all 14 records; this is not an annealer-only improvement.
10_pre_post_milp_provenance: Paired bars show provenance of selected contacts before and after MILP; numbers above bars are actual contact counts. Each stage has its own denominator because schedule cardinality may change. These are provenance shares, not identities carried forward: MILP replaces a component solution and can select different contacts. Full pre/post counts and weights are exported in comparison_metrics.csv.
11_terminal_profile_cost_quality: Only the terminal-sensitivity profiles on the identical frozen 200/50 input are compared. Labels are logical variable/coupler limits. Total reads measure sampling workload, excluding classical reduction/decomposition/verification cost. Per-terminal budgets differ (MWIS 500, CSP 1,000), and changing both caps changes the decomposition itself; this is an observed profile tradeoff, not an isolated effect of increasing reads or a runtime Pareto claim.
12_leaf_size_distributions: Empirical cumulative distributions over all recorded non-empty terminal leaves and incomplete leaves, including alternative separator states; these are workload distributions, not repeated-run uncertainty. Sizes are remaining candidate contacts/binary variables, excluding fixed choices. In the current one-hot/domain-wall encodings one bit is used per contact alternative. Common logarithmic x limits expose large unresolved pieces concealed by average terminal size. Missing incomplete leaves are not plotted as zero-sized observations. Couplers missing in CSP incomplete-leaf metadata remain blank in leaf_metrics.csv.
13_schedule_gantt_s100_g50: Matched final MWIS/CSP schedules for 100/50, terminal limits 30/200. Both panels use the same gateway order and frozen four-hour horizon. Contact colors share the 0–100 operational-weight scale. Required setup intervals are drawn only between successive selected contacts, excluding a trailing reservation after the last contact. Empty gateways remain visible. Equal objectives need not imply identical contact choices or timings. This is the simplified single-antenna, at-most-one-contact-per-satellite model.
14_gateway_contacts_s100_g50: Final selected contacts per gateway for 100/50, limits 30/200. Zero-contact gateways remain included. Since every selected contact lasts four minutes and each station has one antenna, the right axis converts counts to service occupancy over the four-hour horizon. Occupancy excludes setup, visibility availability and idle time; low occupancy is constrained by the one-contact-per-satellite model and is not a measurement of real Starlink network efficiency. Contact counts, minutes, weight and occupancy for every gateway are exported in gateway_metrics.csv.
